headline: Attackers piled onto freshly disclosed enterprise flaws in Microsoft SharePoint, Cisco firewalls, and VMware vCenter as a stealth operation quietly drained Salesforce and ServiceNow data worldwide for 17 months.

emerging_trends.text: Researchers keep turning artificial intelligence inward on its own plumbing, this time replaying encrypted reasoning objects across OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google sessions to recover API keys and passwords from provider logs.

Unauthenticated guest access has become the pried-open side door of software-as-a-service, and the City-Forum operators walked through it to pull records from Salesforce and ServiceNow tenants for 17 months undetected.

North Korea's Lazarus group keeps mining the hiring process, pairing fake job offers and a trojanized PDF reader with a fresh Windows zero-day to plant the ForestTiger backdoor across defense contractors.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Lazarus Windows Zero-Day and Operation Dream Job

topics.title: Actively Exploited Enterprise Flaws
topics.latest_developments: Hackers began weaponizing Rapid7's proof-of-concept for SharePoint flaw CVE-2026-55040 within a day of its Tuesday release, extending a wave in which Cisco ASA and FTD CVE-2026-20349 crash firewalls remotely and VMware vCenter CVE-2026-59310 grants persistent code execution.
topics.summary: Three widely deployed enterprise products now face live attacks: Microsoft SharePoint Server, Cisco Secure Firewall ASA and Threat Defense, and Broadcom VMware vCenter. Apply the vendor patches immediately and hunt for signs of prior compromise.

sources.title: Hackers leverage new Microsoft SharePoint exploit in attacks
Cisco ASA and FTD Flaw Exploited in the Wild Can Trigger Remote DoS
Attackers Exploit VMware vCenter Vulnerability to Gain Persistent Remote Access

topics.title: Critical Vendor Patches Beyond Patch Tuesday
topics.latest_developments: Adobe shipped fixes for three CVSS 10.0 bugs led by ColdFusion operating-system command injection CVE-2026-48362, SonicWall patched critical unauthenticated remote code-execution flaws in its discontinued GMS platform, and Ivanti closed remotely exploitable Endpoint Manager defects that leak external SQL credentials.
topics.summary: A fresh round of perfect and near-perfect severity flaws hits Adobe ColdFusion, Commerce, and Campaign Classic, SonicWall GMS, and Ivanti EPM, several allowing unauthenticated code execution. Administrators should patch or retire the affected servers, especially internet-facing ColdFusion and GMS installs.

sources.title: Adobe Patches Three CVSS 10.0 ColdFusion and Campaign Classic Flaws
SonicWall Patches Critical Vulnerabilities in Discontinued GMS Platform
Ivanti EPM Update Patches Remotely Exploitable Flaws

topics.title: Lazarus Windows Zero-Day and Operation Dream Job
topics.latest_developments: Check Point tied the fresh Windows zero-day to Lazarus's Operation Dream Job, in which the North Korean crew poses as recruiters, ships trojanized PDF software carrying a Lockheed Martin job decoy, and installs the ForestTiger backdoor against defense targets, and CISA gave federal agencies two weeks to patch.
topics.summary: Lazarus lures IT and defense-sector workers with fabricated job openings, then chains a full-control Windows zero-day into persistent access. Defense contractors and their suppliers should patch the flagged Microsoft bug and treat unsolicited recruiter attachments as hostile.

sources.title: Lazarus hackers pair fake job offers with Windows zero-day exploit
Fresh Windows Zero-Day Exploited in North Korean Cyberattacks
CISA gives federal agencies two weeks to patch Microsoft bug exploited in DPRK campaign

topics.title: Aviation Systems Draw Attack Research
topics.latest_developments: Wired reported researchers can open an exterior hatch on a Boeing 737 in under 60 seconds, plug in a coin-sized device, and redirect the autopilot or sabotage the flight plan, while Delta Air Lines and FBI Atlanta opened a probe into a rogue Wi-Fi network and deauthentication attack aboard a Las Vegas-to-Atlanta flight carrying DEF CON attendees.
topics.summary: New work exposes physical and wireless attack paths against commercial aviation, from a hardware implant that hijacks a 737's autopilot to a fake hotspot that knocked passengers off in-flight Wi-Fi. No arrests have followed the Delta incident, and the FBI's Atlanta field office continues to investigate.

sources.title: This Coin-Sized Device Can Hack a Boeing 737
Delta probes Wi-Fi deauth attack on flight carrying DEF CON attendees
DEF CON crowd suspected in fake-hotspot attack on Delta flight

topics.title: City-Forum Drains Salesforce and ServiceNow
topics.latest_developments: Reco disclosed City-Forum, a campaign that abuses unauthenticated guest access to quietly enumerate and exfiltrate data from Salesforce and ServiceNow tenants worldwide for 17 months, run from a rented German server tied to a domain first registered in 2002.
topics.summary: The operators pull records through portals configured to allow guest users, a design many administrators leave open by default. Organizations should audit guest permissions on both platforms and lock down public-facing communities.

sources.title: A stranger has been reading Salesforce and ServiceNow portals worldwide for 17 months
Stealthy 'City-Forum' Attacks Target Salesforce and ServiceNow With Custom Toolset

topics.title: Cross-Vendor AI Reasoning API Leak
topics.latest_developments: Researchers showed that the encrypted reasoning objects OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google pass between reasoning-API calls can be replayed from one session into another, letting a weaker model decode a stronger model's hidden reasoning and recover API keys and passwords from session logs.
topics.summary: The flaw sits in how the three providers carry hidden chain-of-thought between calls, exposing internal reasoning and embedded secrets. Teams building on these reasoning APIs should rotate any keys handled inside prompts and watch vendor advisories for fixes.

sources.title: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google API Flaw Let Weaker AI Models Decode Stronger Models' Reasoning

business_politics.title: July Inflation Eases to 3.4%
business_politics.latest_developments: The July consumer-price index rose 3.4% year over year, matching forecasts, as falling gasoline prices offset lingering fallout from the Iran war.
business_politics.summary: U.S. consumer prices climbed 3.4% in the year through July as pump prices declined, and the dollar and Treasury yields slipped after the reading while stocks opened higher, the print keeping Federal Reserve rate-cut hopes alive even as the Iran war reverberates through the economy.

sources.title: US inflation falls to 3.4% in July
Stock Market Today: Dow Opens Higher After CPI Meets Forecasts

business_politics.title: OPEC Cuts Oil-Demand Forecast as Hormuz Stays Shut
business_politics.latest_developments: OPEC again lowered its 2026 global oil-demand growth forecast as talks to reopen the Strait of Hormuz stalled, and crude futures fell on the absence of any imminent deal.
business_politics.summary: The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries cut its forecast for global oil-demand growth for a second time, citing the closed Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea risks that keep choking supply; the waterway carries roughly a fifth of the world's oil, and its shutdown amid the Iran war has left crude volatile.

sources.title: OPEC Cuts Oil-Demand Forecast Again as Hormuz Talks Stall
Crude Futures Move Lower Awaiting News on Hormuz Talks

business.title: Pennsylvania Rewrites Mineral-Rights Law
business.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported that Pennsylvania quietly enacted a law undermining a state court decision governing ownership of lucrative underground mineral rights.
business.summary: Pennsylvania passed legislation that undercuts a recent court ruling on who owns valuable oil-and-gas mineral rights, a shift that reshapes who collects royalties from the deposits beneath Western Pennsylvania land.

sources.title: Pa. quietly passed a law undermining a court decision on lucrative mineral rights

business.title: Pittsburgh Restaurant Week Returns
business.latest_developments: Pittsburgh Restaurant Week returned with discounted and special-menu meals at dozens of area restaurants, WPXI reported.
business.summary: Pittsburgh Restaurant Week is running deals at dozens of restaurants across the region, the recurring promotion that draws diners to participating kitchens with lower-priced and prix-fixe menus.

sources.title: Pittsburgh Restaurant Week returns with discounted meals at dozens of locations

around_town.title: Emmerling Park Adds Accessible Trail
around_town.latest_developments: Indiana Township officials said a third phase of accessibility upgrades will extend a wheelchair-friendly sidewalk through Emmerling Park.
around_town.summary: Indiana Township is expanding a wheelchair-friendly walkway into its third phase at Emmerling Park, opening more of the site's 120 acres to visitors who use wheelchairs.

sources.title: Wheelchair-friendly sidewalk to be expanded through Emmerling Park in Indiana Township

around_town.title: Monessen Tables Adelphoi Classroom Plan
around_town.latest_developments: The Monessen City School District tabled a motion that would let Adelphoi run a behavioral program in the middle school's sixth-grade wing.
around_town.summary: The Monessen City School District held off on a proposal to give the Adelphoi youth-services agency classrooms in the middle school's sixth-grade wing for a behavioral program, WTAE reported.

sources.title: Monessen school board tables motion that would allow Adelphoi program in middle school

around_town.title: Perseid Meteor Shower Peaks Tonight
around_town.latest_developments: Forecasters said the Perseid meteor shower peaks the night of Wednesday, August 12, with the display lingering into late August.
around_town.summary: The annual Perseid meteor shower reaches its peak over Western Pennsylvania on the night of Wednesday, August 12, and stays visible through the end of the month, WPXI reported.

sources.title: Perseid Meteor Shower peaks Wednesday night, could create colorful display over next few weeks

events.title: Little Italy Days Opens Thursday in Bloomfield
events.latest_developments: WPXI reported the 26th annual Little Italy Days runs Thursday, August 13, through Sunday, August 16, along Liberty Avenue in Bloomfield.
events.summary: The 26th annual Little Italy Days brings food vendors, music, and Italian-American culture to Liberty Avenue in Pittsburgh's Bloomfield neighborhood from Thursday, August 13, through Sunday, August 16.

sources.title: Pittsburgh Little Italy Days kicks off Thursday

around_teams.title: Skenes Puzzled by Pirates' Slide
around_teams.latest_developments: Paul Skenes told the Post-Gazette he is unsure why the Pirates are not playing up to their standard as the second-half slide deepens.
around_teams.summary: Pirates ace Paul Skenes said he cannot explain why Pittsburgh has stopped playing to its standard as the club's second-half losing streak drops it further in the National League Central, per the Post-Gazette.

sources.title: With the Pirates reeling, Paul Skenes is unsure ‘why we’re not playing up to that standard’

team_usa.title: FIFA Overturns Balogun Red in US-Belgium Tie
team_usa.latest_developments: Youri Tielemans said FIFA's decision to suspend United States forward Folarin Balogun's red card helped inspire Belgium in their World Cup knockout tie against the U.S., ESPN reported.
team_usa.summary: Belgium midfielder Youri Tielemans said FIFA's surprise move to overturn Folarin Balogun's red card fired up his side in their World Cup knockout match against the United States men's national team, a call that drew scrutiny to the officiating in the U.S. co-hosted tournament.

sources.title: Tielemans: Balogun red overturn inspired Belgium
